title: Composable VPC edge-fabric Terraform module for private deployments
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Deliver a single, opinionated Terraform module that exposes a composable 'edge-fabric' for Redwood Private VPC deployments. The module should manage subnet layout, IGW/NAT Gateway provisioning, VPC endpoints (interface and gateway), route tables, network ACLs, tagging, and a pluggable health-check layer. It must be usable as a drop-in for new private deployments and support safe upgrades for existing stacks.

Scope:
- Core resources: aws_vpc, aws_subnet (public/private/isolated), aws_internet_gateway, aws_nat_gateway / NAT gateway high-availability pattern, elastic ips, aws_route_table, aws_route_table_association, aws_vpc_endpoint (gateway: S3, DynamoDB where applicable), aws_vpc_endpoint_interface (Secrets Manager, KMS, ECR, STS), aws_flow_log, aws_network_acl.
- Outputs for downstream modules: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, isolated_subnet_ids, nat_gateway_ids, endpoint_ids, route_table_ids.
- Config flags: enable_cross_az_nat (pattern: one NAT per AZ), endpoint_policy_map (per-service JSON blobs), enable_flow_logs, flow_log_destination, tagging_map, tenancy_mode, enable_ipv6 (opt-in).
- Health checks: lightweight probe for endpoints and NAT egress; integration with Console metrics (CloudWatch) and a small Lambda-based reachability check that verifies DNS resolution and HTTP reachability for configured endpoints. A Terraform null_resource triggers smoke checks during apply when plan_ok=true.
- Upgrade/migration strategy: module versioning (major/minor), resource address stability, migration helpers that detect existing NATs/IGWs and import them, and an optional mode that leaves legacy route tables untouched for manual migration. Documented runbook and automated state import script (terraform import wrapper).

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- We avoid introducing proprietary networking constructs that break customers' existing IP addressing; instead provide sane defaults and constraints.
- To maintain deterministic state we will favor explicit resource names and tags; dynamic generated names will be minimized except for EIP allocations.
- High availability pattern uses one NAT Gateway per AZ (cost vs. availability trade-off configurable).

Acceptance criteria:
- Module has >80% unit/acceptance test coverage in Terratest harness that runs in CI.
- Can create a new VPC with recommended defaults in a single apply (<15 minutes) and produce the documented outputs.
- Upgrade test: run module major.minor -> major.(minor+1) change that adds interface endpoints without replacing existing subnets or VPC resources.
- Health checks publish metrics to CloudWatch and create Console dashboard links in README.
- PR reviewed and merged with at least one infra eng + security approval.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module code under infra/modules/vpc-edge-fabric (root module + examples).
- Terratest suite and CI job (pipeline/integration/vpc-edge-fabric).
- README with usage, upgrade runbook, and troubleshooting playbook.
- Example private-deploy stack using the module and showing endpoint polices for S3 and KMS.

Notes on backward compatibility and stateful upgrades:
- Where possible, use aws_eip resource per NAT to allow explicit import of pre-existing EIPs. Provide 'existing_nat_map' input to map AZ->nat_id to avoid replacement.
- Provide 'manage_igw' boolean to allow adopting an existing IGW instead of creating a new one.
- For VPC endpoint upgrades, we will create interface endpoints with explicit security group attachments; if a customer's SG prevents attachment, the terraform plan will surface a clear diff with remediation steps.

Observability & Health checks details:
- CloudWatch alarms for NATGateway: HighActiveConnections, NatGatewayBytesOut (thresholds configurable).
- Endpoint reachability Lambda: resolves endpoint DNS from within private subnets using VPC resolver and performs TCP/HTTPS handshake to service endpoint. Results stored in a DynamoDB table and aggregated into CloudWatch metrics.
- Flow logs aggregated into an S3 bucket or CloudWatch Logs depending on 'flow_log_destination'.

Security considerations:
- All endpoint policies must be reviewed in security PR. Provide default least-privilege policies for ECR/S3 usage by Redwood control-plane.
- KMS endpoints are created only if kms_endpoint_enabled=true and require an allowlist of KMS key ARNs.

Documentation links and artifacts:
testing_plan: Terratest integration job with AWS ephemeral accounts. Tests: create/destroy cycle, endpoints smoke test, upgrade path test (v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0), import test for existing NAT/IGW. CI job should run on merges to main and nightly canary runs.
migration_plan: 1) Identify stacks using legacy module and run terraform plan with manage_igw=false and existing_nat_map populated. 2) Run terraform import for NAT/IGW resources using provided script. 3) Apply module in adopt mode; validate resources and health checks. 4) Flip manage_igw=true if desired and remove legacy module. Document rollback steps in runbook.
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: create new VPCs with module for internal staging first, run health checks for 48 hours. Next apply to a small set of customer-like stacks (canary). Monitor NAT and endpoint metrics; if issues, revert using TF state snapshots. For existing stacks use import mode then reconcile over 1 maintenance window per region.

notes: Aim to keep module surface area opinionated but not prescriptive. Prioritize deterministic names and stable outputs to reduce churn in downstream modules.
